'''William Herbert King'''<ref>[http://recordsearch.naa.gov.au/SearchNRetrieve/Interface/DetailsReports/ItemDetail.aspx?Barcode=6244456&isAv=N KING WILLIAM HERBERT]</ref> (17 August 1920 – 23 August 1990)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://australianfootball.com/players/player/Billy%2BKing/6621|title=Billy King – Player Bio|publisher=Australian Football|access-date=21 November 2014}}</ref> was an [[Australian rules football]]er who played for [[Sydney Swans|South Melbourne]] in the [[Australian Football League|VFL]] during the 1940s. King, who started his career at South Melbourne in 1940, was recruited from Ascot Vale.

Primarily a wingman, he participated in the famous [[1945 VFL Grand Final|1945 'Bloodbath' Grand Final]] which South Melbourne lost to Carlton. In 1947 he represented Victoria at the [[1947 Hobart Carnival|Hobart Carnival]] and was selected in the [[All-Australian Team|''Sporting Life'' Team of the Year]].

King was runner up to Bill Williams in South Melbourne's 1946 best and fairest award.<ref>{{cite web |title=1946 - Bill Williams Wins South's Award |url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/245526770 |publisher=The Herald |access-date=8 March 2021 |pages=24 |date=5 September 1946}}</ref>

King was captain / coach of the [[Corowa Football Club]] in the [[Ovens and Murray Football League]] in 1949 and 1950.<ref>{{cite web |title=1949 - Corowa Football Club |url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/162549400/19823835# |via=Trove Newspapers |work=The Emerald Hill Record |date=26 March 1949|page=7}}</ref>

King played in the New South Wales state team against Western Australia at the Sydney Cricket Ground in June, 1949.<ref>{{cite web |title=1949 - NSW v WA state team |url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/18119832 |via=Trove newspapers |work=The Sydney Morning Herald |access-date=10 April 2020 |date=21 June 1949|page=8}}</ref>

King also played for New South Wales against Victoria in July, 1949, at the Sydney Cricket Ground.<ref>{{cite web |title=1949 - NSW v Victoria |url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/18122292 |via=Trove Newspapers |work=The Sydney Morning Herald |access-date=10 April 2020 |date=13 July 1949|page=8}}</ref>

After two years at Corowa, King accepted the role of captain / coach at [[North Albury Football Club]] in the [[Ovens and Murray Football League]] from 1951 to 1953.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/236927693|title=Corowa Farewells Bill King |via=Trove Newspapers |work=The Corowa Free Press |date=13 March 1952|page=3}}</ref> King was runner up in the 1952 Morris Medal with 19 votes, won by Wodonga's, [[Norm Webb]] on 22 votes.<ref>{{cite web |title=1952 - O&MFL - Morris Medal |url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/236928617 |via=Trove Newspapers |work=The Corowa Free Press |date=26 August 1952|page=4}}</ref>

King also represented the [[Ovens and Murray Football League]] on numerous occasions during his five years as coach of Corowa and North Albury.<ref>{{cite web |title=1953 - O&MFL v Bendigo FL Teams |url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/117131124 |via=Trove Newspapers |work=The Riverine Herald |date=2 June 1953|page=3}}</ref>

In 1954, King was captain / coach of the [[Howlong Football Club]]<ref>{{cite web |title=B. King to captain Howlong |url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/65509272 |work=Benalla Ensign |date=29 October 1953|page=10}}</ref> 
when they won the [[Hume Football League]] premiership, undefeated.<ref>{{cite web |title=1956 - Hume FL Grand Final review |url=https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/236357879 |via=Trove Newspapers |work=The Corowa Free Press |date=7 September 1956|page=3}}</ref>

In 1956, King won the [[Hume Football League]] best and fairest award, the Azzi Medal for Howlong with 21 votes.<ref>{{cite web |title=1956 - Hume FL - Azzi Medal |url=http://www.howlongspiders.com.au/history/achievements/ |publisher=Howlong FNC |ref=1956}}</ref>
